hero.title:
The two-pane
legend reborn
hero.lead: Two panels, function keys along the bottom, a plugin for everything - the working style power users build their habits on, running natively on Windows 11. Born from the open source Open Salamander codebase and written in C++, it now speaks full Unicode, handles long paths, keeps directories open in panel tabs, connects over SFTP, shows source code and Markdown on F3, mirrors your cloud sync status - and ships in a dark theme as well as the light one.
hero.note: Windows installer · Windows 11 · x64 · free under GPLv2

features.title: Old habits, nothing to relearn.
features.lead: A file manager for people who navigate by keyboard and think in two panels.
features.card1Text: Source on the left, target on the right - and each panel keeps several directories open in tabs. Copy, move, pack and compare without opening a second window or reaching for the mouse.
features.card2Text: Function keys along the bottom edge, a shortcut for everything, a command line that stays exactly where your hands already are - and a Command Shell key that opens the shell you choose, from PowerShell to Git Bash.
features.card3Text: tandemcommander.exe is a program with its own identity: own icon, own window titles, own settings - and a modern core built for Windows 11, with full Unicode and long paths throughout.
features.card4Text: Source and configuration files with syntax highlighting in over 200 formats, rendered Markdown, images, databases and executables - F3 opens the right viewer, Alt+F3 the plain one.
features.card5Text: A Linux server over SFTP in one panel, your disk in the other. In cloud folders the panels show the same sync badges as Explorer - OneDrive, Google Drive - with TortoiseGit and TortoiseSVN status next to them.
features.card6Text: A one-time utility brings your hot paths, FTP bookmarks, user menu, colours and plugin settings over from Altap Salamander. Install with the signed installer; a winget package is on its way.

project.title: Open source, and open about how it is made.
project.text1: Tandem Commander grew out of Open Salamander, the classic file manager whose source was opened to the world, and it owes that project everything it started with. Our thanks go to the original Salamander authors and to everyone who kept the code alive after them - a quarter century of careful work by people who cared how a file manager should feel. The core has since gone its own way, but the debt stands.
project.text2: Tandem Commander is free software, licensed under GPLv2 and later. Individual files and bundled libraries carry different but compatible licenses, and everyone who has contributed to it is credited in AUTHORS.
project.text3: The rules the project holds itself to - build reproducibility, incremental modernization, a commitment to Windows, and a stable plugin API - are written down in the repository rather than kept in someone's head.
project.agenticNote: There is one genuinely new thing here. Development follows spec-driven principles: every change starts as a written specification that is clarified, planned and broken into tasks before any code is touched, and the implementation is carried out by agentic coding frameworks. The whole paper trail is committed next to the code, so the repository records not only what changed in this quarter-century-old C++ codebase, but why.

story.title: Why This Project Exists - A Personal Note
story.p1: Whenever I have worked on Windows, there has always been a Salamander close at hand. First Servant Salamander, later Altap Salamander - in my view one of the finest pieces of software I have ever worked with. But the last released version of Altap Salamander dates back to 2019, and it still carries a few aches inherited from the original versions: incomplete encoding support, missing long directory and file path support, and quite a few others. At the same time, many of my friends and family members use Altap Salamander every day, both at work and at home.
story.p2: The moment Salamander was released as Open Salamander, I had a clear vision: I would adapt it for myself so I could simply keep using it. That vision quickly ran into hard reality - even though I am a very experienced software engineer, developer, and architect, I was missing the one factor a project of this scale demands above all else: time.
story.p3: That has changed, essentially within the last few months, with the overall shift in how software can now be - not programmed, but created - with agentic systems. To be clear, I am emphatically not talking about "vibe coding"; I consider that a bit of a buzzword and I do not like it. The term I would choose is Full Agentic Spec-Driven Development: clearly defined procedures not just for producing code, but for producing the entire project - documentation and artifacts included. This project is deliberately built with the spec-driven approach on top of GitHub SpecKit, using the frontier models available at the time.
story.p4: Tandem Commander is, of course, not perfect. But thanks to this approach I ended up with a genuinely usable tool - one that I hope can serve others as well.
story.p5: None of this would exist without the people who built Servant Salamander, Altap Salamander, and finally Open Salamander. Over a quarter of a century they created and refined a program that countless people - me, my friends, my family - have trusted with their daily work, and it shows in every detail: the speed, the keyboard-first design, the plugin architecture, the sheer care in the code this repository inherited. Their decision to release it under an open-source license was an act of real generosity that gave this remarkable software a second life. Tandem Commander stands entirely on their shoulders, and I hope it honors what they built. To all the original authors and contributors: Thank you.

pad.desc450: Tandem Commander is a fast, keyboard-friendly two-pane file manager for Windows 11, born from the open source Open Salamander codebase. Each panel keeps several directories open in tabs, names are full Unicode and paths may exceed 260 characters. It connects to Linux servers over SFTP, shows source code with syntax highlighting and rendered Markdown on F3, displays cloud sync badges, and has light and dark themes. Free under GPLv2 or later.
pad.desc2000: Tandem Commander is a fast, keyboard-friendly two-pane file manager for Windows 11. It carries on the classic orthodox file manager working style: source panel on the left, target on the right, function keys along the bottom edge, a shortcut for everything, and a command line that stays exactly where your hands already are. Each panel can keep several directories open in tabs, browser-style: every tab remembers its own view, sort order, filter, selection and history, and the whole set is restored at the next start. The program was born from the open source Open Salamander codebase and now runs on its own modernized core built for Windows 11: names and paths are Unicode end to end, so accents and non-Latin scripts render correctly everywhere, and paths past the old 260-character limit just work. An SFTP plugin puts a Linux server in one panel and your disk in the other, with password or private-key authentication, host-key verification and unix permissions shown directly in the panel. Pressing F3 on a source or configuration file opens the Code Viewer with syntax highlighting for more than 200 languages and formats in twelve colour schemes; on a Markdown file it opens a rendered view with headings, lists, tables and code blocks; the image viewer and fast, correctly rotated thumbnails handle large photo folders. In cloud-synced folders the panels show the same sync-status badges as Windows Explorer, and TortoiseGit and TortoiseSVN badges appear next to them. The Command Shell key opens the shell you choose - Command Prompt, PowerShell, Windows Terminal, Git Bash or any program. A one-time utility migrates hot paths, FTP bookmarks, the user menu and plugin settings from Altap Salamander. The classic light look remains the default, and a dark theme offers the same layout and information density. Tandem Commander is free software, open source under GPLv2 or later, with the full source code, issue tracker and all releases available on GitHub.
